advances: Proves the arbitrary-polygon equal-quarter cap rigidity needed by the round-034 calibration argument. The proof establishes the stronger inequality \(|C_0|\ge\min_i|C_i|\), with equality only for a triangle cut by its three medial lines.
author: mp_r35_quarter_rigidity
proof:
Each \(L_i\) meets the interior of \(Q\) in a nondegenerate chord, since both \(C_i\) and \(C_0\) have positive area. The part of \(\partial Q\) lying strictly in \(H_i^+\) is one connected polygonal chain. The three such cap chains are disjoint and occur cyclically on \(\partial Q\). Between every two consecutive cap chains there is a polygonal chain contained in \(C_0\), possibly reduced to one point.

Replace each of these three central boundary chains by the chord joining its endpoints. The region removed by such a replacement lies in \(C_0\), because \(C_0\) is convex. After all three replacements one obtains a convex polygon \(Q'\) such that its three caps are still exactly \(C_1,C_2,C_3\), while its central cell \(C'_0\) satisfies \(C'_0\subseteq C_0\).

The three new central chords are supporting sides of \(Q'\). If one is a point, choose a supporting line there between the two one-sided supporting directions. Thus zero-length central boundary intersections remove no area and still supply a support. Extend the three supporting lines. In the nonparallel case their halfplanes containing \(Q'\) bound a triangle \(P\supseteq Q'\). The corner cap \(P_i=P\cap H_i^+\) contains \(C_i\). Moreover,
\[
P_0=P\cap H_1^-\cap H_2^-\cap H_3^-=C'_0.
\]
Indeed, both polygons are bounded successively by the same three cutting-line chords and the same three new central supporting sides.

We now prove the required inequality for the triangle \(P\). Label its vertices \(v_1,v_2,v_3\) so that \(P_i\) is the corner at \(v_i\). On the edge \(v_iv_j\), let \(x_{ij}\) be the fraction of that edge from \(v_i\) to its intersection with \(L_i\). Pairwise disjointness gives
\[
x_{ij}+x_{ji}\le 1.
\]
Writing \(A=|P|\), the cap areas are
\[
|P_1|=x_{12}x_{13}A,\qquad
|P_2|=x_{21}x_{23}A,\qquad
|P_3|=x_{31}x_{32}A.
\]

Set
\[
a=x_{12},\quad b=x_{21},\quad
c=x_{13},\quad d=x_{31},\quad
e=x_{23},\quad f=x_{32}.
\]
Thus \(a+b\le1\), \(c+d\le1\), and \(e+f\le1\). Assume, after relabeling, that \(ac=\min\{ac,be,df\}\). Then
\[
ac\le (1-a)e,\qquad ac\le(1-c)(1-e).
\]
Hence
\[
1\ge \frac{ac}{1-a}+\frac{ac}{1-c}.
\]
After multiplying by \((1-a)(1-c)\), this becomes
\[
(1-a)(1-c)\ge ac(2-a-c).
\]
The difference of the two sides factors as
\[
(1-a)(1-c)-ac(2-a-c)=(ac-1)(a+c-1).
\]
Since \(ac<1\), it follows that \(a+c\le1\).

Interchanging indices \(2\) and \(3\) if needed, assume \(c\ge a\). Also
\[
be+df\le (1-a)e+(1-c)(1-e)=1-c+(c-a)e.
\]
If \(c\le1/2\), then
\[
2ac+be+df\le2ac+1-a\le1.
\]
If \(c\ge1/2\), the inequality \(ac\le(1-c)(1-e)\) gives \(e\le1-ac/(1-c)\), and therefore
\[
\begin{aligned}
2ac+be+df
&\le 2ac+1-c+(c-a)\left(1-\frac{ac}{1-c}\right)\\
&=1+\frac{a}{1-c}\left(ac-\bigl(c^3+(1-c)^3\bigr)\right).
\end{aligned}
\]
Since \(a+c\le1\),
\[
ac\le c(1-c)\le c^3+(1-c)^3,
\]
where the last difference is \((2c-1)^2\). Thus again \(2ac+be+df\le1\). Consequently,
\[
|P_0|
=A(1-ac-be-df)
\ge Aac
=\min_i|P_i|.
\]

Equality is possible only when every inequality above is an equality. In the case \(c\le1/2\), equality forces \(c=1/2\); the positive lower bound on \(1-e\) then forces \(a=c\). In the case \(c\ge1/2\), equality forces simultaneously \(a+c=1\) and \((2c-1)^2=0\). Thus in either case \(a=c=1/2\). The two minimum inequalities then force \(e=1/2\), and equality in the three edge constraints forces
\[
a=b=c=d=e=f=\frac12.
\]
Hence the three cutting lines are exactly the medial lines of \(P\).

If two selected supporting sides are parallel, regard their intersection as a vertex at infinity and approximate them by supporting sides meeting arbitrarily far away on the cap side. The resulting bounded triangles have central and cap areas converging to those of \(Q'\). The preceding inequality passes to the limit. Zero-length central chains are handled by the supporting-line choice above. Equality cannot occur only in such a limiting configuration: with \(ac\) minimal and \(c\ge a\), the preceding estimates give
\[
\frac{|P_0|-|P_1|}{|P_1|}
\ge\frac{1-2c}{c}
\quad\text{when }c\le\frac12,
\]
and
\[
\frac{|P_0|-|P_1|}{|P_1|}
\ge
\frac{c^3+(1-c)^3-ac}{c(1-c)}
\quad\text{when }c\ge\frac12.
\]
Thus a ratio tending to equality forces \(a,c\to1/2\); the minimum constraints then force all six edge fractions to tend to \(1/2\). The limiting support triangle is therefore bounded and medial. This also proves the equality characterization in every degenerate boundary case.

Combining the reduction with the triangle inequality gives
\[
|C_0|\ge |C'_0|=|P_0|
\ge\min_i|P_i|
\ge\min_i|C_i|.
\]
If equality holds, every inclusion and every area inequality in this chain is an equality. No positive-area central ear was removed, every \(C_i\) fills its triangular cap \(P_i\), and all six edge fractions equal \(1/2\). Hence \(Q=P\) is a triangle and the cuts are its medial lines.

Under the quarter-area hypotheses, \(|C_0|=\min_i|C_i|=|Q|/4\), so the equality characterization applies.
statement:
Let \(Q\subset\mathbb R^2\) be a two-dimensional compact convex polygon. For \(i=1,2,3\), let \(H_i^+\) be a closed halfplane, let \(L_i=\partial H_i^+\), and put \(C_i=Q\cap H_i^+\). Suppose the interiors of \(C_1,C_2,C_3\) are pairwise disjoint and
\[
C_0=Q\cap H_1^-\cap H_2^-\cap H_3^-,
\]
where \(H_i^-\) is the complementary closed halfplane. If all four sets have positive area, then
\[
|C_0|\ge \min\{|C_1|,|C_2|,|C_3|\}.
\]
Equality holds if and only if \(Q\) is a triangle and the \(L_i\) are its three medial lines, with \(C_i\) the three corner triangles. Consequently, if all four areas equal \(|Q|/4\), then \(Q\) is a triangle and the cutting lines are its medial lines.
